_schema.description: Candidates for both houses. Seeded from the 30 Oct 2026 research report. scripts/refresh.py adds Wikipedia names as 'announced' without changing existing rows, then applies the ABC election guide, the primary lower-house source: ABC-listed candidates become 'endorsed', and an ABC entry supersedes any other row for the same party and seat (the older row is kept with status 'superseded', never deleted). From 9 Nov 2026 the VEC's official list (scripts/vec_nominations.py, vec_nominations.json) decides who is standing: every candidate on it is a vec_nominated row with its ballot position, and a row it doesn't list is withdrawn ('did not nominate'). After that, Wikipedia and the ABC add no rows.

fields.district: id of the district in districts.json (Legislative Assembly); null for Legislative Council rows
fields.region: Legislative Council rows only: id of the region in regions.json
fields.name: Candidate name
fields.party: Party code (ALP, LIB, NAT, LNP, GRN, ONP, VS, AJP, ND, WEST, SAL, LBT, FF, LCV, SUS, DLP, SFF, IND, OTH)
fields.status: vec_nominated (on the VEC's official list, from 9 Nov 2026) | endorsed (preselected or endorsed by the party, or listed in the ABC guide) | reported (reported, not independently verified) | announced (listed on Wikipedia, added automatically) | withdrawn (withdrew, or not on the VEC's list at the close: notes say 'did not nominate') | superseded (replaced by an ABC entry for the same party and seat) | not_standing (not a 2026 candidate: a row entered in error, kept with a note saying why, hidden like superseded rows)
fields.ballot_position: Position on the ballot paper (Assembly; for the Council, the position among all the region's candidates) once the VEC publishes its 9 Nov draw, else null
fields.ticket_position: Council rows: place within the group once the VEC publishes the draw; before that, as reported
fields.incumbent: Assembly: true if this is the sitting member
fields.source: vec (added from the VEC's list of nominations) | abc (listed in the ABC guide) | wikipedia (added from Wikipedia) | electiontracker (found through electiontracker.au's reconciliation report and added by hand; source_url is the party or campaign page it cites) | absent for rows from the research report or entered by hand from a news report (cited in source_url)
fields.source_url: Where the row came from (the ABC district page for source abc)
fields.website: Assembly: the candidate's website as linked from their ABC guide card (usually the party's candidate page), when listed
fields.date_added: YYYY-MM-DD the row was added by refresh.py (Melbourne date)
fields.superseded_by: superseded rows: name of the ABC entry that replaced this one
fields.superseded_on: superseded rows: YYYY-MM-DD it was superseded
fields.updated: YYYY-MM-DD the row was last checked
fields.notes: Optional: backing (e.g. Climate 200), source conflicts or other caveats
fields.group: Council rows: the group's letter on the ballot once the VEC publishes the draw (null when ungrouped or not yet published)
fields.ballot_name: vec_nominated rows: the name exactly as on the VEC's list and the ballot ('SURNAME, Given')
fields.vec_url: vec_nominated rows: the VEC nominations page that lists the candidate
fields.party_name: Rows coded OTH: the party as the VEC prints it
fields.former_names: Earlier spellings in the tracker before the VEC's (the candidate id, profile and photo moved to the new spelling)
fields.withdrawn_on: withdrawn rows: YYYY-MM-DD the row was marked withdrawn
fields.moved_to: withdrawn rows of a person who nominated for another seat: their candidate id there
